## Today

`ExerciseSessionSystemImpl.startExerciseSession()` (line 45) calls
`exerciseClient.getCurrentExerciseInfoAsync().await()` before the
function's own `try` block, which starts at line 52. An exception from
this call propagates unhandled instead of resolving to
`ExerciseSessionStartOutcome.Failed` the way the rest of the function
already does for `startExerciseAsync`.

`PlatformModule.provideHealthConnectClient()` (line 43) checks
`HealthConnectClient.getSdkStatus(context)` inside a `try` (lines
38-42) and returns `null` on failure, then calls
`HealthConnectClient.getOrCreate(context)` outside any `try`, in a
Hilt `@Provides` method. An exception thrown there fails Hilt's graph
construction, at application start, outside any screen able to report
it — the guard against an unusable Health Connect SDK exists, but the
call it is meant to protect sits outside it.

`HrPermissionSystemImpl.isGranted()` (line 32) calls
`healthConnectClient.permissionController.getGrantedPermissions()`
with no `try` anywhere on that path; an exception propagates unhandled
to whatever calls `isGranted()`.

## Expected

`ExerciseSessionSystemImpl.startExerciseSession()` moves the
`getCurrentExerciseInfoAsync().await()` call inside the function's
existing `try`, so a failure there also resolves to
`ExerciseSessionStartOutcome.Failed` — the same failure-as-a-value
outcome the function already returns for the calls after it (R33).

`PlatformModule.provideHealthConnectClient()` wraps
`HealthConnectClient.getOrCreate(context)` in the same `try` (or an
equivalent one) as the `getSdkStatus` check, and returns the same
`null` sentinel this function already returns for an unavailable SDK,
instead of letting the exception cross the `@Provides` boundary (R33).

`HrPermissionSystemImpl.isGranted()` wraps
`getGrantedPermissions()` in a `try`, and returns `false` — the
"not granted" outcome the function's own return type already
expresses — on failure, instead of letting the exception propagate
(R33).
